meta.title: Next Session — Candidate Scenes
meta.subtitle: The GM's working slate for the 22nd (into Fall 1224), built on three spines: Wilhelm's delivery run to Scarem Montem, Dagmar's push into the regiones gated behind Tormente, and Confluensis turning the screws on the home front. The Carnac material is now backed by a full five-level site brief (see meta.source_briefs) — scenes s8–s10 have been rewritten against it and s15–s18 added for the deeper levels. Forward-looking only — beats played in the 2026-08-08 session have moved to the Chronicle and the Open Questions. Derived from the Open Questions prep hub (q027, t078).

source_briefs.title: The Carnac Regio — GM Brief
source_briefs.scope: Five nested Magic-aligned levels beneath the drowned end of the Carnac alignments. Discovered by Dagmar, Spring 1224. Playable 1224–1226.

campaign_clock.detail: Jupiter and Saturn close to 2.1 arcminutes in Aquarius — an evening-sky event, the closest observable great conjunction between 1226 and 2020. It does not unlock a chamber; it makes the level-5 crossing survivable for one night. Hang the lock on the PATH, not the aura: Magic auras do not fluctuate cyclically.
campaign_clock.runway: Fall 1224 → March 1226 — roughly six playable seasons.
campaign_clock.player_facing: Dagmar's established method is premonitions plus astrology, so the date is his to discover in character. Aldebaran (a Behenian fixed star) is the anchor the conjunction points at; the Hyades are the classical rainy stars, which matches the covenant's maritime regio grammar.
campaign_clock.optional: Halley's Comet passed in 1222 — usable in retrospect as what woke the lower levels and produced the 1224 mirror-flash.

corrections: 2026-08-19 — The Diedne Garden is on the SOUTH COAST OF THE ENGLISH CHANNEL, not within the Ránargarðr holding on the Isle of Man. Earlier s13 text asserting otherwise has been struck.
2026-08-19 — Scarem Montem left the 1223 Tribunal with the Latin manuscript of Wilhelm's thesis and has held it for roughly a year by the time of the delivery. See s6.
2026-08-19 — Valdemar's Isle-of-Man site carries a MAGIC AURA OF 3 (confirmed). Recorded in s13.

scenes.title: What Wilhelm's assistants bring back — and can it break the thesis?
scenes.hook: Wilhelm's research assistants return from the winter gathering (sent west and south, paid in grain and silver). The live beat is whether any of it FALSIFIES the folk-magic thesis rather than confirming it.
scenes.detail: ADVANCED (Summer 1224): Carl & Isaac returned — the technique worked but the madness cost was realized (a suicide and a double killing among ~12-15 students); the temporal mage's brass ACORN turned up with no magic residue. The weak maritime citation is still unfilled, and still gates the delivery (s6). A negative result — a tradition that works without leaning on the environment, or the missing open-ocean storm-prediction / current-finding citation turning out not to exist — forces Wilhelm to revise before he can deliver to Scarem Montem (see s6). Developed: the negation is a MADNESS failure rate that breaks the scalable / vis-factory case without disproving the magic itself; the assistants also flag a temporal hedge mage who beat the Limit of Time, leaving Wilhelm an origin-less brass acorn.

scenes.title: Éogan and the capricorn
scenes.hook: On the voyage home from Ireland a Magic-realm capricorn (sea-goat) singles Éogan out and paces his ship — offered as his first familiar prospect. The work is courting it and the binding lab-work, not an instant bond.
scenes.detail:
ADVANCED (Spring 1224): Éogan spotted the capricorn at a river-mouth near Drogheda (it favours salt-meets-fresh water), took a water sample and cast a relocation spell. Courtship and binding are still ahead. Developed: the draw is independent of the 'small fae drawn to Éogan/Stijntje' affinity; its signature specialty is CROSSING THRESHOLDS INTO REGIONES (mythic grounding in Enki's Goat-Fish and Macrobius's Gate of the Gods). Corpus build/bind references and a suggested Might ~12–16 Magic build are recorded. What it wants in exchange remains open.

CARNAC LINK: per the site brief's backstory cascade, the fae were driven WEST into Atlantic and Irish waters c. 225 AD. Éogan's fae attendants (t068) and a Magic capricorn offering itself at an Irish river-mouth are both downstream of the same displacement — a player character is standing in the far end of the Carnac backstory without knowing it.

scenes.title: The Carnac ladder — five levels, and the inversion
scenes.thread: The dragon errand / the Carnac regio
scenes.hook: Umbrella frame for the whole Carnac arc. Five nested Magic levels under the drowned alignments. The party will enter believing the goal is to reach level five. By the time they understand the building, the goal is to make sure it never opens.
scenes.detail:
THE LADDER (Regio Sight Roll: Per + appropriate Ability + stress die vs EF 5 + 2× aura difference; Second Sight, Magic Sensitivity, or the InVi lvl-3 boundary guideline — Vision target gives the route):
  L1 The Cave — aura 7 — EF 7 — Tormente resident, tidal.
  L2 The Alignments — aura 8 — EF 9 — the sightline apparatus.
  L3 The Colony — aura 9 — EF 7 — murfolk; social gate.
  L4 The Throne Room — aura 10 — empty, waiting.
  L5 The Road — 10+ — not a room; conjunction only.

Auras are built from RoP:Magic tethers, not asserted: caves/water/astrological alignment on the natural side (cap 5), the megalithic monument at 1 per century of active use on the preternatural side (comfortably capped at 5 by a millennium of murfolk worship). Level 1 is the ONLY level where a living creature does any of the work.

THE WALL: the mechanical wall and the social wall are the same wall. Level 3 is the only floor from which level 4 can be reached, and the murfolk own it.

NON-LINEARITY: the lock is operated from level 2 but acts on level 5, so the party must fight up, learn what the lock is, and come back DOWN to set it — crossing level 3 twice, with the murfolk's disposition possibly changed in between.

REACH ON THE 22nd: levels 1 and 2 are plausibly in play. Level 3 is the pacing wall and probably the session's end. Levels 4–5 are staged (s17, s18) and should stay out of reach.

OFFSTAGE BACKSTORY (do not resolve here): c. 225 AD Jörmungandr shifted position; the fae were displaced west into Atlantic waters; the merfolk were squeezed out of the sea and retreated UP into the already-ancient Carnac stack. None of the three tiers knows about the tier above it. The correction is a millennium away and out at sea.

scenes.title: Confluensis turns the screws — the Grand Tribunal complaint
scenes.hook: The home-front spine for the 22nd: after the public 13th-place "Siege of Shame" at the 1223 Tribunal and Bertrand's cold renege of the book-storage deal, Confluensis moves from soured silence to active reprisal — assembling a complaint against Sjórseiðr while the covenant's magi are scattered north (Dagmar/Valdemar) and south (Wilhelm).
scenes.detail: The documented direction (c022): someone from Confluensis is preparing to bring Rán's open faerie association — and the covenant's OTHER exposed edges — before the Grand Tribunal as a bundled quaesitorial complaint. Live edges it could gather: Valdemar parading the sea-fae Rán at the feast (c022), the unspendable five bags of stolen Roman dragon-gold and its provenance (c026), Mímormr loosed toward the North Sea by Dagmar's errand (t072), and — most dangerous — Wilhelm's ungifted folk-magic teaching with its madness/death toll (t019, t020, q028). Oleron, a Liege that favours Sjórseiðr for beating the other lieges, is the natural counter-ally (t074). What FORM the screw-turning takes first — a formal charge, a whispering campaign, vassal-poaching, or economic pressure through the soured Bertrand arrangement — is the live beat. GM prep 2026-08-09 (t078). Planned opening gambit (t078, 2026-08-15): a FORGED Order-of-Odin letter, manufactured to implicate Valdemar and entered as evidence — details TBD.

scenes.title: The Diedne Garden — a druidic circle on the Channel coast, and the road to initiation
scenes.thread: Vis sources / the Diedne Garden / Valdemar's lineage
scenes.hook: Valdemar has taken on the covenant's newly-won Diedne Garden — a Herbam vis source (3 pawns/yr) on the SOUTH COAST OF THE ENGLISH CHANNEL, not on the Isle of Man. It is an old druidic circle. He can spend the season there harvesting, or he can spend it beginning to initiate himself into the Diedne mystery.
scenes.detail:
CORRECTION OF RECORD: the garden is on the Channel's south coast. Earlier notes placing it inside the Ránargarðr holding on Man were wrong and have been struck from s13.

WHY THE SITING IS BETTER: it sits in the Tribunal's heartland, not on a private island. It was won as a Tribunal prize, so its location is a matter of public record — everyone in Normandy knows who holds it. Every season Valdemar spends there is a season a DIEDNE SITE is being visited, repeatedly, by a magus from the covenant Confluensis is building a case against (s11). Part of the ordeal is simply being seen going.

AND IT COSTS HIM SEASONS: Undrahöll on Man (s13), the garden on the Channel, and the raiding that funds both are three different places. He cannot do all of it. Making him choose between his laboratory and his lineage every year is the engine of this thread.

═══ THE INITIATION ═══
The Diedne are a thousand years dead, so there is no mystagogue. THE SITE IS THE MYSTAGOGUE — the script is kept in the circle, recoverable a rung at a time, and the Ordeals are things the place demands rather than things a person imposes. Give Valdemar a DIEDNE LORE cult ability to accumulate; each season in the garden is a script attempt.

THE LADDER (four rungs, capstone deliberately years out):
1. THE NAMING — Outer Mystery. He says his lineage aloud inside the ring, which is the first time he has said it to anything. Grants Diedne Lore 1. Ordeal cost: minor.
2. THE GREEN SEASON — a modest grove-bound working benefit (study or spontaneous bonus within the circle).
3. THE BENDING — a partial capstone, usable years early: reduce an opponent's Penetration by his Diedne Lore score. Lets him feel it working before he has earned the whole thing.
4. THE UNBROKEN RING — Major Hermetic Virtue. HALVE an opponent's Penetration total against him.

BALANCE NOTE: halving Penetration is very strong — against a Penetration 40 attack that is a flat −20 on top of Parma. Purely defensive, so it does not warp offence, but it will make him near-unhittable by anything short of a Tribunal. Two tunings, pick one:
  (a) BIND IT TO THE RING — it functions only inside a circle he has consecrated, including small ones he can lay in a season or scribe aboard a ship. Thematically exact, self-limiting, and it makes his HOLDINGS the source of his power rather than his person.
  (b) UNCONDITIONAL, PRICE IN THE FLAWS — TMRE convention is one Flaw per script. For a secret Diedne the right Flaws are not personal hardships but LEGIBILITY: his magic begins resisting in a way no catalogued Hermetic Virtue explains. RECOMMENDED — because Confluensis is assembling a bundled complaint (s11), an anomalous resistance is not a rumour but a demonstrable effect a quaesitor can test for, and Valerian is a former Rhine quaesitor sitting at his own dinner table. The capstone virtue becomes the confession.

STILL TO PREP: the Herbam harvest mechanics (season/window, roll, botch risk); whether a guardian, ward, or standing condition sits on the harvest; and what the long-dead Diedne planter left behind. Valdemar also means to pick up basic Herbam in order to work it.

STANDING NOTE: Valdemar is secretly House Diedne (t078). Stacked with the Christian lie (s14) and the fief, this is the highest-stakes exposure any PC carries.

scenes.title: Valdemar bargains for the land — and the Christian lie
scenes.hook: Rǫgnvaldr Guðrøðarson (Reginald), the Christian King of Mann and the Isles, grants Valdemar right and title to the Ránargarðr holding — potentially as a proper feudal fief — but the grant demands he profess himself a Christian, which is a lie.
scenes.detail: The stage-able beat behind Valdemar's Isle-of-Man holding (see the thread t081). Much of the groundwork is backstory the covenant doesn't know about — a favour already done for King Rǫgnvaldr, a down payment made in goods or services, title received in writing — so this can play as the formal grant and the moment of the lie, or as a later reveal to the covenant. Live beats: whether he swears an Oath of Fealty (not his preference) or bargains a promise of specific service instead; what that owed service is (a standing debt the GM can call in — t081); and how far the Christian lie widens his exposure, stacking on his hidden House Diedne lineage (t078). Around it, Ránargarðr / Nóatún is growing into a Viking fjord-town — grog families first, then settlers, then pirates; a Norse bailiff; a winter Althing. Runs straight off s13 (raising the manor and Undrahöll), which now carries a confirmed Magic aura of 3 — low enough that the growing fjord-town can be settled without Warping its people. Note the Diedne Garden is NOT part of this holding; it lies on the Channel's south coast (s12).

scenes.title: Level 3 — the colony, and the negotiation you cannot avoid
scenes.thread: The Carnac regio / the social gate
scenes.hook: Aura 9. Murlocs, not mermaids — croaking, wide-mouthed, bulge-eyed, wattled, wearing salvaged ship-timber as carapace. They hold the only floor from which level 4 can be reached, and have held it for a thousand years.
scenes.detail:
WHAT THEY ARE. A distinct magical species with Magic Might — not warped humans, not transformed anything. Their anatomy is theirs; they were webbed and wattled when they still had the open sea. Treat them as a people, not a condition. They are the natives; the party are the strange-looking ones.

THE MISREADING (and it is a mistake the party can make honestly). A magus who sees a webbed, water-adapted grog on level 1 and a colony of webbed, water-adapted beings on level 3 will draw the obvious line. It is false — convergent adaptation to the same aura, not shared ancestry — and voicing it will insult them badly, because they know exactly what they are and have never been anything else.

WHAT THEY BELIEVE. There is a king on the floor above. He took them in when the fae drove them from the water. They tend his threshold and have done so for forty generations; he will rise when they are finally owed. They are correct that he will rise. Everything else is wrong. They do not have a history — they have a grievance, polished into liturgy, which they chant, and which is misdirected by two whole tiers.

THE PRISON, NOT THE SANCTUARY. Tormente does not let things out. The murfolk have been inside a sealed vessel for a thousand years with a guardian at the door that will not release them and does not consider them the point. So they do not want help going UP — they want help getting OUT. Level 3 is a prison bargain, and the party is the first thing in ten centuries to walk in the front door with any prospect of walking back out.

RUNNING IT. The party must cross level 3 twice — up, and back down to set the pillars — and their standing can change between crossings. The thing they must not say is the one thing that would break the murfolk entirely. Whether the party works out what is upstairs BEFORE or AFTER they need murfolk cooperation is the single biggest pacing decision in the whole arc.

COVENANT HOOK: the salvage-as-carapace register deliberately echoes the hermit crab wearing half a hull at the Scandinavian sea-mount (Spring 1222). If Dagmar makes that connection out loud, it is a real piece of scholarship.

scenes.title: Level 4 — the throne room, and the thing that is not in it
scenes.hook: Aura 10. Empty. Waiting. A throne room for a king the murfolk think is theirs. It is Hastur's. STAGED — should not be reachable on the 22nd.
scenes.detail:
REALM ASSIGNMENT — the key design decision. Do NOT file him under Infernal: that flattens him into a duke of Hell in a mask and, worse, makes him legible. Put him in the TWILIGHT VOID — RoP:M's second part of the Magic Realm, sparse and foreboding, home to ancient beings it is wisest not to disturb, and given no bestiary in the published text. Claiming that address costs nothing.

TWO BENEFITS: (1) it stays Magic-aligned, so the magi are not eating doubled botch dice in the throne room — DE clarifies that the doubling applies in a regio whose realm differs from that of the POWER; (2) it gives a delivery vector requiring no travel at all. Magi who go into Twilight go into the Void. A bad botch, a Warping-heavy season, and someone meets him without leaving the lab. That horror is free from the system — and Dagmar is currently at Warping 0 with Weird Magic, which is a fuse worth lighting slowly.

WHAT IS IN THE ROOM: nothing. An absence with the shape of an occupant. A seat, maintained, running on habit, tended by a congregation who have not been told anything. The mark on the floor is not fae — that is where the murfolk's liturgy fails.

THE YELLOW SIGN AS REGIO PATH. DE explicitly allows entry by following a particular path or ritual. The Sign fits that slot — and it PROPAGATES. The moment the party writes it down, sketches it in a lab text, or describes it to a Redcap, the regio acquires a new door. Their own scholarship is the vector, which is a very Ars Magica failure mode and lands squarely on a covenant that trades in books.

scenes.title: Level 5 — the road, and the March 1226 lock
scenes.hook: Not a room. The far side. The conjunction of 4–5 March 1226 does not unlock a chamber — it makes the crossing survivable, for one night.
scenes.detail:
RoP:M notes that gateways into the Magic Realm proper are guarded by fierce creatures on the FAR side and typically open inward only; insulae are theorised as Magic regiones above aura 10, and aura 10 already reads in core as a gateway to the realm of its affiliation.

THE INVERSION, stated plainly: the goal is not to reach level 5. It is to be standing in the throne room in March 1226 and prevent the stairs from appearing — while the only people who know the building are convinced the party has come to rob their church.

HANG THE LOCK ON THE PATH, NOT THE AURA. Magic auras do not fluctuate cyclically; the aura stays 10 and only the stairs are conditional. DE's Ease-Factor language covers this explicitly.

LLEWELLYN'S PRIZE (§10). RoP:M gives three unprovable models of the Magic Realm — cosms, the Magic Archipelago (insulae and Ferrymen), and tempora (deeper = older; popular with Criamon, which is Dagmar's house). Orkney was already a COSM reading: room-sized spherical microcosms hanging in liquid sky. Carnac in the archipelago idiom is the same phenomenon under a different theory. Two magi, two models, one regio, incompatible maps — exactly the trap Erobos warned about, and exactly the ammunition Llewellyn needs. The published text says sustained exploration by a group of magi MIGHT make one theory harder to sustain, and that the storyguide then decides the underlying truth. That is a campaign-length prize and it is on the table.

OPTIONAL: A. Vibert Douglas identified five conjunctions across 1226–27. If you want the number five doing extra work — five conjunctions, five levels, each keyed to one, the fifth simply the last to arrive.

scenes.title: London — brokering the dragon's gold
scenes.hook: Tormente handed Dagmar a brokerage errand — sell the Roman 'debris' gold on the dragon's behalf. London, the nearest gold market, is where it has to be converted, and the covenant already has form there.
scenes.detail: STUB for next session. The recovered Roman dragon-gold is now Tormente's, and Dagmar owes it a sale. The problem is the one c026 already mapped: a silver-standard economy with no gold coinage, treasure-trove law, and provenance questions — melt to bullion, use a discreet fence / Jewish moneylender / Lombard banker, or commission worked goods. Foxglove knows the London fence from the earlier run (verified events). Live beats: how much of the coin to convert and how (melt vs sell-as-is), what Dagmar reports back to Tormente, and whether the covenant's own Flanders/Bruges bullion channels are now open since the theft is resolved.
